scenes.title: Subnet sizing and growth planning
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates subnet sizing and growth planning with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

Start with the VPC slash sixteen and the two Availability Zones. Each zone has a small public subnet, larger application subnet and dedicated data subnet. The spare ranges are reserved for future growth and additional Availability Zones. The right size comparison demonstrates that a slash twenty-four has two hundred fifty-six total addresses but only two hundred fifty-one usable in AWS, while a slash twenty-two has one thousand twenty-four total and one thousand nineteen usable. AWS reserves the first four and last IPv4 address in each subnet. A subnet CIDR cannot be resized after creation, so replacing a small subnet requires migration planning.
Walk through the real CIDRs, next hops and security constraints
Size for future ENIs, containers, load balancers and AZ expansion, not just current EC2 counts.

For a professional architecture decision, inspect the source and destination addresses, the effective route table associated with the subnet, and the security boundaries. Treat the concrete values in the diagram as a worked example of this decision, not as a configuration that every workload must reuse.

scenes.title: VPC IPAM centralized address allocation
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates vpc ipam centralized address allocation with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

The top of the diagram is AWS VPC IP Address Manager. It allocates from an organization-wide top-level private address pool, then subdivides that range into regional pools for us-east-one and eu-west-one. The lower branches show distinct VPC slash twenty CIDRs drawn from the proper regional ranges. The governance panel explains scopes, allocation rules, tagging, utilization monitoring and sharing pools through AWS RAM. This structure helps avoid overlapping CIDRs before many accounts and Regions become connected. IPAM is an allocation and discovery service, not a router or a mechanism that automatically renumbers old overlapping networks.
Walk through the real CIDRs, next hops and security constraints
Centralize allocation early, verify scopes and pool rules, then investigate existing overlaps separately.

scenes.title: Overlapping CIDR remediation
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates overlapping cidr remediation with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

The left comparison shows two accounts each using ten dot twenty dot zero dot zero slash sixteen. Since both networks advertise the same destinations, direct peering or Transit Gateway routing cannot distinguish their overlapping resources unambiguously. The lower diagrams show migration of the second VPC to a nonoverlapping ten dot thirty slash sixteen, after which routing can be established. Follow the four right-hand stages: inventory dependencies, reserve nonoverlapping space with IPAM, build or migrate resources to the new subnets or VPC, and validate routing, DNS, firewall rules and rollback. PrivateLink can expose selected services without full routed connectivity, but it does not fix overlapping address space.
Walk through the real CIDRs, next hops and security constraints
Prevent overlapping allocations and plan controlled renumbering for full network connectivity.
